description.value: The study examined whether cognitive reappraisal changes neural valuation of positive and negative emotional images, focusing on whether vmPFC activity tracks subjective and normative emotional value.

design.value: Two independent experimental samples of human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI. Exp1 was newly collected, and Exp2 was a replication sample drawn from a previously published study; experimental parameters were nearly identical.

task_description.value: While undergoing scanning, participants completed a cognitive reappraisal task. They were asked to either regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally.

instructions.value: For the Experience condition, participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally. For the Regulate condition, participants were asked to emotionally detach themselves from the image by imagining themselves as an objective observer or imagining the event as having no personal relevance to them.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

task_performance_measures.value: After each trial, participants rated how positive or negative they felt after having implemented the strategy.

task_description.value: Exp2 was a replication sample drawn from a previously published study and used a nearly identical cognitive reappraisal task.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to either regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally. In Exp2, the cues were “Experience” or “Decrease.”

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

task_performance_measures.value: After each trial, participants rated how positive or negative they felt after having implemented the strategy.

description.value: Gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence with standard scanning parameters; FOV = 256 mm; flip angle = 60°; 30 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane. Each run contained 288 volumes of data, with the first six volumes discarded.

Gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence with parameters differing from Exp1 as follows: TE = 31 ms; flip angle = 90°; 34 slices; voxel size = 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.8 mm. Each run contained 238 volumes of data, with the first six volumes discarded.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data; whole brain coverage.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data; whole brain coverage with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.

fMRI data were preprocessed using FSL FEAT. Preprocessing included motion correction, brain extraction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, and normalization to MNI space using each participant's high-resolution anatomical image.

steps.value: Spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM.
Registration to each participant's main structural image using FLIRT with six degrees of freedom.
Registration to standard space using FLIRT with 12 degrees of freedom.
Runs with more than five volumes with movement greater than 1 mm in any direction were discarded.

model_settings.value: One regressor of interest was created for each trial type: Positive-Experience, Negative-Experience, Positive-Regulate, Negative-Regulate, and Neutral-Experience. Nuisance regressors modeled the initial picture presentation and response period. Regressors modeled the 8 s implementation period in Exp1 and 6 s in Exp2.
The data were combined across all runs within a single participant.
The analysis modeled effects across all participants.
Valence and condition were modeled as fixed effects and each participant as a random effect, with a variance components covariance structure.

The model included participants' trial-by-trial ratings of stimulus valence. The parametric regressor was orthogonalized to the main effect, and a quadratic regressor was included to control for nonlinear effects.

A first-level model was created for each trial for each participant using the implementation period. Nuisance regressors modeled all other trials, the initial picture presentation, and the response phase. FSL's motion outlier function identified bad time points, and trials corresponding to those time points were excluded.

The model included experiment number, IAPS normative ratings, condition, the interaction of IAPS normative ratings and condition, and trial-by-trial estimates of pvmPFC activation as independent variables, with trial-by-trial valence ratings as the dependent variable.

model_representation_notes.value: Nuisance regressors were included for the initial presentation of the picture and the response period; first-level models corrected for local autocorrelation, and all regressors were convolved with a standard double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Negative regulation activated regions of the prefrontal cortex including the inferior frontal gyrus, the middle frontal gyrus, and the superior frontal gyrus; regulating negative emotion also led to increased activation in the posterior cingulate and the angular gyrus.

title.value: Effect of reappraisal, IAPS rating, and pvmPFC activation on behavior

footer.value: GLM revealed that IAPS normative rating, condition, and an IAPS normative-rating-by-condition interaction predicted valence ratings. In addition, there was also a significant relationship between pvmPFC activation and behavior. *Significant.

description.value: Reports the behavioral GLM parameter estimates for experiment number, IAPS rating, condition, the IAPS-by-condition interaction, and pvmPFC activation.
